subject: Gaps and large chromosomes after marker ordering in F2 cross map (GBS/RAD-seq data)

messages.author: bcd3aa1722c7fea4
messages.subject: Gaps and large chromosomes after marker ordering in F2 cross map (GBS/RAD-seq data)
parts:
Dear All,

I am quite new to QTL mapping and currently try to construct a genetic map for a plant species from F2 cross.

The background is the following:
The data is represented by 140 F2 progeny individuals + 2 homozygous parents genotyped at all positions, 6310 SNPs after all filtering procedures in TASSEL.
I run all filtering procedures from "genetic map construction" tutorial including filtering for duplicate SNPs and segregation pattern (p < 0.05/#of obs.). As a result I have around 137 individuals and 3K SNPs left, ~150 markers per chromosome on average.
Since I have a prior knowledge on the the linkage groups I did not try to form them from scratch, furthermore by reading the forum I understood that if the genome is assembled one should not try to reconstruct the LGs.
Thus I started to order the markers and for each chromosome I had the following picture:


As you can see there are several gaps with low LOD scores at the ends of the chromosome before ordering and similar gaps in the middle of chromosome after ordering. Furthermore the genetic map is implausibly large ~1200 cM. By the way est.map() produced even worth result thus I refused to use it and used orderMarkers() with Kosambi mapping function (Haldane produced a bit larger map of 1400 cM).

What I already tried to do in order to to remove such gaps:
-remove pairs of distant markers located at more than 30 cM after running allchrsplits()
-remove markers that that demonstrated high LOD scores (>-20) after running droponemarker()
All of these attempts were followed by re running orderMarkers() with Kosambi mapping function. And both of these methods failed to significantly reduce the length of the chromosome.

What I want to do is intuitively get rid of the gaps with low LOD scores, since I guess that these are the reasons for such huge chromosome lengths but I don't know how to do that correctly with R/qtl functions. I suspect that these gaps are the result of noisy GBS data, but despite strict filtering they somehow remain in dataset.

So I wonder if someone already faced such or similar problem with GBS data analysis? And what were your solutions to remove such "noisy" markers and fix the chromosome length?

Sincerely,
Rim

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Gaps and large chromosomes after marker ordering in F2 cross map (GBS/RAD-seq data)
parts:
If you have information about marker order from a physical map, you should use that rather than try to re-order markers from scratch.

The function orderMarkers() is crude. And note that it calls est.map() repeatedly.

From your plot of the pairwise linkage information, it looks like you have two chunks of markers that are linked to each other but not linked to the markers in the middle (that off-diagonal rectangle of yellow in the second figure). So you may need to move around markers by hand.

Large gaps in the estimated map mean adjacent markers show high recombination fractions. You want to try to figure out whether it's an individual marker that is the problem, or a problem with marker order.

karl

And in case If I still want to try to fix the genetic map from what point should I start and what criteria should be used to do? messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Gaps and large chromosomes after marker ordering in F2 cross map (GBS/RAD-seq data)
parts:
I would start with your physical map, and use some estimate of the cM/Mbp relation for your organism to get an approximate genetic map.

If you want to re-estimate the inter-marker distances with your genotype data, it's better to start with the physical order. Determining order from scratch should bring you back to the same place, and you'll still need to estimate the inter-marker distances.

The data cleaning to fix problems in the estimated map can be difficult. I guess I'd first look at segregation distortion. Then I'd look at the markers adjacent to any huge intervals: if you drop one of those markers, does the interval shrink? This is what the droponemarker() is supposed to help with.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Gaps and large chromosomes after marker ordering in F2 cross map (GBS/RAD-seq data)
parts:
In R/qtl, use est.map(). It takes the order as fixed and uses maximum likelihood to estimate the inter-marker distances, It uses a hidden Markov model, allowing for the presence of genotyping errors.

karl
